top.title: PSHAN, WHO urge increased private investment to rescue Nigeria’s healthcare system
top.description: By Matthew Johnson The Private Sector Health Alliance of Nigeria (PSHAN) and the World Health Organisation (WHO) have called for increased private sector investment and stronger public-private partnerships to address persistent challenges confronting Nigeria’s healthcare system. The organisations said government alone could not shoulder the responsibility of transforming the health sector, stressing that sustained private sector investment was critical to improving healthcare delivery, strengthening infrastructure and achieving universal health coverage. The call was made at the 2026 PSHAN Annual Gala and Awards Night held in Lagos on November 20, with the theme, “Legacy Builders: Honouring the Visionaries of the Nigerian Healthcare System.” Speaking at the event, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of PSHAN, Dr. Tinuola Akinbolagbe, said the alliance was working to position the private sector at the centre of Nigeria’s health development through strategic partnerships, investment, innovation and institutional strengthening. She said PSHAN was seeking to move beyond fragmented private sector interventions towards coordinated investments capable of strengthening health systems and delivering measurable and sustainable outcomes. According to her, meaningful progress in healthcare requires shared responsibility and collaboration across different sectors. “As we look towards 2027 and beyond, our ambition is to move from fragmented contributions by the private sector to coordinated investment, from isolated interventions to stronger health systems, and from good intentions to measurable, sustainable outcomes,” she said. Akinbolagbe explained that the theme of the event was designed to celebrate individuals, institutions and organisations whose courage, leadership, innovation and commitment had contributed to shaping the future of healthcare in Nigeria. In his keynote address, former President of the African Development Bank Group and Executive Chairman of the Global Africa Investment Summit, Dr. Akinwumi Adesina, described healthcare as an investment in human capital and essential economic infrastructure rather than merely social sector expenditure. Speaking on the theme, “Health as Wealth: Mobilising African Leadership and Capital to Build Sustainable Health Systems,” Adesina said a healthy population was fundamental to productivity, innovation, economic competitiveness and national prosperity. He maintained that no country could achieve sustainable wealth without a healthy population, insisting that investment in healthcare was essential to building a productive workforce and inclusive economy. Adesina called for stronger partnerships between government and the private sector, noting that government alone could not finance and deliver the transformation required in the country’s healthcare system. He urged businesses to move beyond philanthropy and corporate social responsibility initiatives to embrace healthcare as a strategic investment

top.title: Buffalo Sabres Could Offer Red Wings Another Dylan Larkin Trade Path
top.description: The Detroit Red Wings have a Dylan Larkin problem, and the Buffalo Sabres might have something that could help solve it. Unfortunately for Detroit, there’s one rather significant obstacle standing in the way: Larkin himself. Buffalo has been linked to the former Red Wings captain for weeks, with NHL insider Chris Johnston reporting that the Sabres made a substantial offer for the 30-year-old center. But while Buffalo’s collection of young talent could make it an attractive trading partner, Larkin has reportedly refused to include the Sabres among his approved destinations. That leaves Detroit staring at an intriguing possibility it cannot currently pursue without the player’s cooperation. Oct 22, 2026; Vancouver, British Columbia, CAN; Detroit Red Wings forward Dylan Larkin (71) skates against the Vancouver Canucks in the second period at Rogers Arena. Mandatory Credit: Bob Frid-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Buffalo Sabres Reportedly Made Significant Dylan Larkin Offer According to Chris Johnston’s reporting, detailed by The Hockey Writers , Buffalo submitted what was described as a significant offer for Larkin earlier this month. The exact proposal has not been publicly confirmed, but the interest appears to be legitimate. TSN insiders Pierre LeBrun and Darren Dreger have also identified Buffalo as a team interested in acquiring the Michigan native. However, Dreger indicated that Larkin was unlikely to approve a move to the Sabres, creating a major obstacle for both organizations. That remains the central problem in Detroit’s effort to navigate Larkin’s limited trade list . A compelling offer means very little if the player refuses to authorize the move. And with Larkin carrying a full no-movement clause, the Red Wings cannot simply send him to Buffalo because they like the return. Could Buffalo’s Young Centers Interest Detroit? Here’s where things become interesting from Detroit’s perspective. The Sabres have several young centers who could potentially fit the Red Wings’ long-term plans, including Noah Ostlund, Konsta Helenius, and Jiri Kulich . All three were listed on Buffalo’s opening-season roster, although Helenius was placed on injured reserve on November 12. Ostlund might be particularly intriguing because of his offensive upside, although Buffalo’s commitment to him complicates any hypothetical deal. The 22-year-old signed an eight-year, $52.8 million extension in September, demonstrating that the Sabres view him as an important part of their future. Helenius, meanwhile, offers another potential young-center option, while Kulich has shown promise as an offensive contributor. There is no confirmed report that Buffalo has offered any of these players for Larkin, but they illustrate why the Sabres could be an interesting trading partner. top.title: ‘Give him the Heisman’: Opposing coach praises Jeremiah Smith after Ohio State loss
top.description: Oct 17, 2026; Bloomington, Indiana, USA; Ohio State Buckeyes wide receiver Jeremiah Smith (4) lines up pre-snap during the first quarter against the Indiana Hoosiers at Merchants Bank Field at Memorial Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Robert Goddin-Imagn Images Nebraska picked up the biggest win of Matt Rhule’s tenure on Saturday, beating No. 14 Ohio State 31-28 in Lincoln and likely ending the Buckeyes’ College Football Playoff hopes. But even after the win, Rhule had plenty of praise for the opponent’s biggest star. Rhule said that Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith should win the Heisman Trophy, and that he’s never competed against a player as “talented and special.” Nebraska Upsets Ohio State Nebraska jumped out to a 21-7 lead in the second quarter, but Ohio State battled back to tie the game at 21 in the third quarter. The Huskers then pulled away in the fourth quarter on a 33-yard field goal and a 26-yard touchdown pass, before holding on after a late Buckeyes touchdown. Smith did his part, finishing with 165 receiving yards and two touchdowns, including a 67-yard score on Ohio State’s first drive. But the Buckeyes managed just 76 rushing yards, while Nebraska ran for 176. The loss drops Ohio State to 7-4, and it’s the Buckeyes’ latest setback in a frustrating season. Smith drew criticism earlier this month when one longtime Ohio State reporter called him “ a petulant child ” for his frustration on the sideline during the team’s loss to Oregon. For Nebraska, which also improved to 7-4, it was the program’s first win over Ohio State since 2011. ‘Give him the Heisman’ While the Buckeyes might have lost the game, Rhule didn’t hesitate to praise Ohio State’s biggest during his on-field interview with Fox’s Jenny Taft after the game. “Jeremiah Smith, give him the Heisman. I mean, we doubled him,” Rhule said . He doubled down during his postgame press conference. “I don’t think I’ve ever competed against a player as talented and special — and I’ve had a chance to play against a lot of them — than that kid Jeremiah Smith. That man, he is unbelievable, the way he can absolutely just tilt a game,” Rhule said . Smith is widely considered the top player in college football. While Ohio State has fallen out of the College Football Playoff conversation in recent weeks, Smith has remained at or near the top of the Heisman Trophy odds. Rhule seems to think it would be well-deserved if he took home the hardware next month. top.title: Mathew Barzal’s return has been an Islanders boost — even if it involves some rare patience
top.description: Barzal DETROIT — Three games into his return from injury , Mathew Barzal is, perhaps with a veneer of caution, feeling good. His minutes, as you’d expect being on the third line, are down over four minutes per night, but he’s produced a point per night with good underlying numbers, albeit over a small sample. It is, in short, as good as the Islanders might have expected after Barzal missed the season’s first 18 games with lingering knee issues from an injury suffered two seasons ago. “Not bad,” Barzal told The Post before the Islanders faced Detroit on Saturday. “It’s gonna take a second just to get my legs and cardio back. Just timing and everything. I think I’ve been fairly solid. Feel pretty comfortable out there. Especially the Columbus game. I feel pretty similar to last year.” That is an interesting coda, as Barzal said upon his return that he felt at 80 percent for much of last season, and was managing his knee extensively in between games. Much like it has so far this year, though, that didn’t seem to impact his production, as Barzal had 72 points in 81 games and averaged the most ice time of his career. New York Islanders center Mathew Barzal (13) skates with the puck against the Columbus Blue Jackets on Tuesday, Nov. 17, 2026, at UBS Arena in Elmont, N.Y. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect While the Islanders will almost certainly look to boost Barzal’s workload at some point soon if everything keeps going well , they are in the luxurious situation of not needing to rush. Their top two lines are humming along well, and they have enough depth down the middle that the matchup advantage created by Barzal being on the third line is something coach Pete DeBoer has been happy to have in his pocket. “I think he’s getting better every night,” DeBoer said. “I like his mindset. He’s playing a mature game for us as far as with the puck and not trying to push too much, which is the natural instinct when you come back. You want to make a difference. He’s a difference-making guy. But he’s picking his spots. He’s got good patience in his game.” Patience hasn’t always been Barzal’s M.O., but — whether related to his knee or not — he does seem to be playing a more concise game. His average shift length, for example, is down by five seconds compared to last season, though that could be affected both by a small sample and by DeBoer’s bench management, which has seen drops in that statistic throughout the lineup. Perhaps the biggest difference with Barzal back in the fold is simply the added depth it gives the Islanders lineup, and the subsequent confidence that seems to give everybody. Being able to slot Jean-Gabriel Pageau on the fourth line, and send Calum Ritchie to AHL Hamilton for a de facto rehab assignment — Ritchie featured in a 2-0 loss to Belleville on Friday, notching five shots on goal — are things most teams in the NHL simply couldn’t do. So too is letting Barzal return on the third line, with fewer minutes, as opposed to tossing him right back

top.title: Maple Leafs Healthy Scratch Veteran In Surprising Move
top.description: Oliver Ekman Larsson Maple Leafs Getty The Toronto Maple Leafs, who have lost eight straight games, made a surprise decision for their lineup on Saturday night. The Maple Leafs take on the Columbus Blue Jackets on Saturday in what is a must-win game. If they are going to win, then they will need to do so without one of their veteran defenseman. Maple Leafs Scratch Oliver Ekman Larsson According to Maple Leafs head coach Jim Hiller, the team has decided to shake up its lineup by making veteran defenseman Oliver Ekman Larsson a healthy scratch. “Jim Hiller confirms Oliver Ekman-Larsson is a healthy scratch for Leafs tonight,” wrote TSN reporter Mark Masters on his X. Jim Hiller confirms Oliver Ekman-Larsson is a healthy scratch for Leafs tonight @TSN_Sports — Mark Masters (@markhmasters) November 21, 2026 We knew that the Maple Leafs were going to make some changes to their lineup after losing eight games in a row, but it’s still surprising to see the team give a healthy scratch designation to Ekman Larsson. Despite his struggles this season, Ekman Larsson has been a staple of the Maple Leafs’ defense since he joined the team two years ago, so this is a big surprise to see him as a healthy scratch. Maple Leafs Could Have Traded Oliver Ekman Larsson Last Year At last season’s trade deadline, former Toronto GM Brad Treliving was said to have multiple trade offers on the table for Ekman Larsson, who was having a great season for Toronto. But he decided to hold onto him instead of trading him. That looks like a big mistake in hindsight, as Ekman Larsson only has one assist in 24 games this season, compared to 8 goals and 39 points last year in 74 games. The Maple Leafs likely would have gotten a draft pick or two for him at last year’s trade deadline, but now, his trade value is gone, and the Maple Leafs may have to actually attach an asset to move his contract out following this healthy scratch. Ekman Larsson is owed $3.5 million this year, and next year, as part of his four-year, $14 million free-agent contract he signed after he left the Florida Panthers. The deal was looking good for the Maple Leafs at first, but not anymore. top.title: 49ers veteran receiver’s recent departure hints at Mike Evans’ imminent return
top.description: The San Francisco 49ers release Brandin Cooks to make room for a potential Mike Evans return. It’s unknown if Mike Evans will play in the 49ers’ highly anticipated matchup against the Vikings on Sunday, but the team’s latest move indicates a potential return. NFL insider Adam Schefter revealed on Saturday that the 49ers waived veteran wide receiver Brandin Cooks, which would create a spot for Evans. Mike Evans lining up at wide receiver in an NFL game. AP Photo/Jed Jacobsohn Cooks was signed to the 49ers’ practice squad as insurance to help what was an already injury-depleted wide receiver room as the team was without Evans at the time due to a hip injury. On Oct. 1, Cooks was promoted to the team’s active roster, a few weeks before Evans went down with an Achilles injury in Week 6 against the Commanders. This past week, the 49ers have been hinting that Evans could be active for Sunday’s game as he flew to Colorado Springs, Colo. , to practice with the team as it prepared to adjust to the altitude in Estadio Azteca — sitting 7,350 feet above sea level. 49ers wide receiver Deebo Samuel sprinting down the sideline. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Cooks, 33, primarily struggled with San Francisco this season, having only five receptions for 58 yards in five games. Before Evans was injured, he was the team’s leading receiver and was establishing a promising connection with quarterback Brock Purdy, having 27 receptions for 420 yards and three touchdowns through six games. Evans’ looming return to the 49ers’ roster this week comes a week after Deebo Samuel returned from a hamstring injury and had a two-touchdown performance in last week’s 46-40 win against the Cowboys. Deebo Samuel sprinting down the sideline. AP Photo/Tony Gutierrez It’s unknown what the future holds for Cooks. top.title: Miami Heat Vice City Jerseys Spark Massive Resale Frenzy After GTA 6 Launch
top.description: Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images The Miami Heat are riding a wave of pop culture hype that has nothing to do with basketball points. Fans are scrambling to grab limited edition “Vice City” jerseys tied to the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6. These special uniforms have turned into instant collector’s items with prices skyrocketing on the secondary market. The team released the gear for a game earlier this week, and the demand was immediate and intense. Rockstar Games announced that the new video game sold $3.79 billion in just 24 hours. That massive launch created a fever pitch for anything branded with the Vice City name. The Heat jumped on this trend by offering the jerseys to ticket holders for one game only. Scarcity is the key driver here, as fans who missed out are now paying steep prices to own a piece of the moment. Resale Numbers Hit Stratospheric Levels The market for these jerseys moved fast and hard. Data from eBay shows that the top sale for a full bundle including the jersey and shorts reached $2,000 on release day. Three separate sales crossed the $1,000 mark within the first few days. This kind of price jump shows just how desperate some fans are to own the gear. Average prices for the jerseys alone have settled around $300. Sales range from $250 to $400 depending on the listing. In just three days, there were 285 total sales recorded on eBay for the Miami Heat Vice City set. The average sale price for those items sits at $348.57. These numbers prove that the item has value far beyond its retail cost. A New Twist on City Connect Tradition The Heat have a long history of using their alternate uniforms to honor local culture and history. They previously explored the Miami Vice theme in December 2020. This new release takes that concept further by leaning directly into the GTA 6 video game connection. The design features the VICE logo in its final format, blending the game’s aesthetic with the team’s identity. This partnership is part of a broader effort involving Fanatics and the Cactus Jack brand owned by Travis Scott. That brand has already seen success with Topps cards and exclusive releases for Wrestlemania. The collaboration brings a streetwear vibe to the court that appeals to a younger demographic. It also bridges the gap between sports fans and gaming enthusiasts in a way few teams have tried before. The Fear of Missing Out Drives Demand Many fans who want the jersey do not live in Miami or have tickets to the game. This creates a sense of fear of missing out among the wider fan base. The exclusivity of the one-per-ticket holder rule made the item feel rare and special. People who missed the window are now forced to pay a premium to get in on the action. top.title: In epic comeback, Monmouth beats Campbell 55-49 on last-second TD
top.description: Destiny defied Monmouth. The fickle mistress of the football universe plagued the Hawks with officiating errors and self-inflicted mistakes in a crucial season finale on the road against Campbell . But with 39 seconds left and Monmouth trailing 49-47, she offered a glimmer of favor. Quarterback Frankie Weaver heaved a pass that could've been intercepted, and instead the ball bounced off a Camel defender and into the hands of receiver Christian Harrison at the 19-yard line for a 50-yard gain. That break of fate was all it took for the Hawks. Because they're not a product of destiny, they're a force of their own making. And individually, there was no more palpable force than wide receiver Tra Neal. On one final contested fade route, the star redshirt junior would not be denied as he caught the game-winning 17-yard touchdown, his fourth of the day, with 20 seconds remaining to complete Monmouth's incredible 55-49 comeback win over Campbell on Saturday. "This moment—it's as good as they come," Monmouth head coach Jeff Gallo said. "Our guys fought so hard. Resilient in how they finished the game. And they fought together in the fourth quarter specifically. We've had a lot of great wins in this program, and this is just another great one." It was one final instance in a long pattern of resilience and resolve from the FCS No. 20 Hawks. The two teams were tied 28-28 at halftime, but No. 21 Campbell (8-4) surged with 14 unanswered points to take a 42-28 lead into the fourth quarter. Monmouth (9-3) could have conceded after electing to go for a two-point conversion down 42-34 and not getting it, which beget another failed attempt later that left them down 49-40 with 8:03 remaining. "It all blew up in my face. I was aggressive the entire second half. We were gonna be aggressive though. I wasn't gonna sit there and let the clock bleed out," Gallo said. "We were gonna be active participants and win this game, all the way through. Sometimes it goes your way, it didn't. From the onside kick to the blocked punt to the two-point plays. But our guys kept fighting." It seemed as though another decisive blow had beset them when the Hawks cut the lead to 49-47 with less than two minutes left and then recovered a remarkable onside kick, only for the officials to call a non-existent offsides penalty that negated a play that would've turned the tide for Monmouth. But it didn't matter, the force of the Hawks superseded that ill-timed bit of erroneous intervention. Neal produced an exceptional effort in the receiving game with nine catches for 249 yards and four touchdowns. While Weaver was fortunate on that last heave, he was in complete control aside from that play with another spectacular gun-slinging performance that was somehow even better than what he showed the previous week when he was rated as the best passer in the FCS. nigeria.title: PSHAN, WHO urge increased private investment to rescue Nigeria’s healthcare system
nigeria.description: By Matthew Johnson The Private Sector Health Alliance of Nigeria (PSHAN) and the World Health Organisation (WHO) have called for increased private sector investment and stronger public-private partnerships to address persistent challenges confronting Nigeria’s healthcare system. The organisations said government alone could not shoulder the responsibility of transforming the health sector, stressing that sustained private sector investment was critical to improving healthcare delivery, strengthening infrastructure and achieving universal health coverage. The call was made at the 2026 PSHAN Annual Gala and Awards Night held in Lagos on November 20, with the theme, “Legacy Builders: Honouring the Visionaries of the Nigerian Healthcare System.” Speaking at the event, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of PSHAN, Dr. Tinuola Akinbolagbe, said the alliance was working to position the private sector at the centre of Nigeria’s health development through strategic partnerships, investment, innovation and institutional strengthening. She said PSHAN was seeking to move beyond fragmented private sector interventions towards coordinated investments capable of strengthening health systems and delivering measurable and sustainable outcomes. According to her, meaningful progress in healthcare requires shared responsibility and collaboration across different sectors. “As we look towards 2027 and beyond, our ambition is to move from fragmented contributions by the private sector to coordinated investment, from isolated interventions to stronger health systems, and from good intentions to measurable, sustainable outcomes,” she said. Akinbolagbe explained that the theme of the event was designed to celebrate individuals, institutions and organisations whose courage, leadership, innovation and commitment had contributed to shaping the future of healthcare in Nigeria. In his keynote address, former President of the African Development Bank Group and Executive Chairman of the Global Africa Investment Summit, Dr. Akinwumi Adesina, described healthcare as an investment in human capital and essential economic infrastructure rather than merely social sector expenditure. Speaking on the theme, “Health as Wealth: Mobilising African Leadership and Capital to Build Sustainable Health Systems,” Adesina said a healthy population was fundamental to productivity, innovation, economic competitiveness and national prosperity. He maintained that no country could achieve sustainable wealth without a healthy population, insisting that investment in healthcare was essential to building a productive workforce and inclusive economy. Adesina called for stronger partnerships between government and the private sector, noting that government alone could not finance and deliver the transformation required in the country’s healthcare system. He urged businesses to move beyond philanthropy and corporate social responsibility initiatives to embrace healthcare as a strategic investment

nigeria.title: Anambra’s Ekwulobia flyover to be commissioned November 27
nigeria.description: By Vincent Ujumadu The Anambra State Executive Council has fixed November 27, 2026, for the formal commissioning and opening of the Ekwulobia flyover constructed by the administration of Governor Chukwuma Soludo. The flyover is strategically located at a junction that previously experienced serious traffic challenges, particularly during festive periods when vehicular movement increases significantly. Rising from its meeting in Awka, the State Executive Council directed that all necessary arrangements be made to ensure a successful and hitch-free commissioning. However, it did not disclose who would perform the ceremony. The state Commissioner for Information and Value Reorientation, Dr Law Mefor, described the flyover as one of the flagship urban regeneration projects of the Soludo administration. He said the project stood alongside the transformation of Okpoko, formerly regarded as the biggest urban slum in the South-East, into an area characterised by improved infrastructure, order and human dignity. “These projects underscore Governor Soludo’s irreversible commitment to building a liveable, prosperous and smart mega-city in Anambra State,” Mefor said. Meanwhile, the Council resolved to move the state’s Internally Generated Revenue (IGR) drive from moral suasion to full enforcement, including the prosecution of tax evaders, to maximise the state’s revenue potential. It consequently urged residents, business owners and other taxpayers to pay their taxes and levies promptly to avoid the consequences of enforcement, particularly prosecution. According to the Council, no modern state can be built on voluntary compliance alone, stressing that payment of taxes is a civic responsibility. “Anambra will enforce it fairly and firmly,” the Council said. The Council also disclosed that it had concluded work on the state’s 2027 budget, which Governor Soludo is expected to present to the Anambra State House of Assembly on Tuesday. Mefor described the proposed budget as a consolidation budget designed to deepen the gains of Solution 2.0 in infrastructure, security, education, healthcare, youth empowerment and economic transformation. nigeria.title: Makinde’s image on campaign balloon stirs controversy at Tinubu’s Ibadan rally
nigeria.description: By Adeola Badru The image of Oyo State Governor, Seyi Makinde, displayed alongside those of President Bola Tinubu and other political figures on a campaign balloon at the All Progressives Congress (APC) rally in Ibadan on Saturday has stirred controversy, raising questions about the governor’s political alignment ahead of the 2027 general elections. The balloon, hoisted at the rally ground around the historic Mapo Hall, featured images of prominent political figures, including Makinde, who is not a member of the APC and has yet to publicly declare support for Tinubu’s re-election bid. Its appearance attracted attention at the campaign venue, particularly as Makinde is the presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM). The governor’s inclusion on the balloon raised questions about the circumstances surrounding the display and the political message it was intended to convey. However, it was not immediately clear who authorised the inclusion of Makinde’s image or the circumstances that led to its appearance at the APC rally. Meanwhile, President Tinubu has urged residents of Oyo State to sustain their support for the APC, declaring that continuity was essential for Nigeria’s progress, prosperity and development. Speaking at the rally, Tinubu promised increased investments in education, agriculture, industrialisation and electricity supply, while endorsing Senator Sharafadeen Alli as the APC’s governorship candidate in the state. The President also announced plans to revive the old Leyland factory in Ibadan, disclosing that his administration had signed an agreement with Chinese automobile manufacturer, Yutong, to reopen the facility for public transport vehicle production and establish an automobile assembly plant. “For Oyo State, we have just signed an agreement with China’s Yutong to reopen the old Leyland factory in Ibadan. We are reopening it to produce public transport vehicles and establish an automobile assembly plant there. We will continue to bring industries. You will see progress and development,” Tinubu said. He also assured residents of improved electricity supply, expressing confidence in the efforts of the Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe, and his team. “You will see, and I guarantee you an improvement in electricity. Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe is really working hard with his team,” he said. Tinubu urged the electorate to remain committed to the APC, recalling their support for the party in the previous election. “You voted overwhelmingly for APC last time. You must stay the course. You must. For the sake of progress, prosperity of our country, development, for your children and our great-grandchildren,” he said. He stressed the need to prioritise education and agriculture to create opportunities for younger generations. “We must give them the right education, invest in agriculture,” he said. The President also criticised opposition parties, describing them as “mediocre”, and urged voters not to be distracted by them

nigeria.title: Being one step ahead of an opportunist
nigeria.description: By Bunmi Sofola SYLVIA admitted that her parents’ marriage and the stoic way her mum yielded her position as the first wife to a much younger and ambitious woman prepared her for the way she handled her relationship with men. Her story: “When a man suddenly discovers he’s scaled the ladder of success faster than he’d envisaged, what does he do when he gets to the top? Chuck his frumpy wife for a more sophisticated model that’s what! And it happened to my mother – a stark illiterate my father too couldn’t read or write, but he was a fairly successful cocoa farmer and although we weren’t exactly rolling in the lap of luxury, we were the envy of our small town – talk about big fish in a small pond indeed! “My dad had been on the war-path with the leadership of the Pentecostal Church we attended. Things finally got to a head, and he broke away to found his own church. A chunk of the congregation from the former church went with him and in a couple of years, his church had ballooned into something he himself never envisaged. As donations kept on pouring in from far and wide, he built a mini estate, installed my mother and her children (four of us) in one of the chalets, then got married to a school certificate holder and made her his main wife. His excuse was that he needed an educated ally to go through the books of the church and welcome visitors in a presentable way. “I don’t want to go through the rage and resentment we from my mother’s side felt as we witnessed this imposter parade herself as an intellectual. My poor father didn’t know that he was the laughing stock of the congregation who sniggered at the clumsy speeches his ‘educated’ wife always made, riddled with mistakes. “I was lucky to have a sharp brain and qualified as a lawyer. But I wasn’t lucky in my choice of a husband. Eventually my marriage hit the rocks after five years and two children. The man I had my third child for wasn’t much better, but I was lucky to meet this influential projects director of a parastatal and my life changed for the better. He took care of all my financial needs and was almost twenty years older than I was. “It is amazing what some women put up with for money. This man was fat and flabby. Whenever he slept over and I watched him asleep with his mouth so wide open I could see his missing teeth and the fillings in some of the rest snoring away without a care in the world. I felt really repulsed. He was definitely not a sight to light the fire in any virile woman’s loins, but he was kind and generous. nigeria.title: Terrorists kill Niger village head, five others, abduct residents
nigeria.description: …Governor Bago deploys joint security team to affected community By Clare Nnabuike, Minna Suspected terrorists have killed the village head of Lumma Ba’are community in Borgu Local Government Area of Niger State, Mallam Bawa Muhammad, and five other residents in an attack that also left several people abducted and houses burnt. The attackers reportedly invaded the community at about 5:00 a.m. on Saturday, November 21, 2026, shortly after the Muslim call to prayer, forcing residents to flee into nearby bushes for safety. Sources in the community alleged that the assailants beheaded the village head and burnt his body. They also reported that a newborn baby died after being left inside a house that was set ablaze during the attack. Several residents were reportedly abducted, although the exact number of those taken away had yet to be established. Some residents also alleged that individuals from the community had collaborated with the attackers. However, the claims had not been independently verified as of the time of filing this report. The Niger State Police Command confirmed the attack, saying five people were killed and that joint security teams had been deployed to the area to apprehend the perpetrators. The Police Public Relations Officer, Wasiu Abiodun, said in a statement that the incident was reported at about 5:00 a.m. on November 21. “On 21/11/2026 at about 5am, report received indicated that suspected armed men invaded Lumma Ba’are village, Borgu LGA and attacked the community, while about five persons reportedly lost their lives during the attack. “Joint security teams have been deployed to the location, efforts to apprehend the suspected perpetrators ongoing. Further development will be communicated,” Abiodun stated. Also confirming the incident, the Niger State Commissioner for Information and Orientation, Obed Nuhu Nana, said five other persons sustained injuries and were evacuated to the General Hospital, New-Bussa, where they were receiving medical attention. In a statement, Nana said the attack occurred amid lingering intercommunal tensions in the area, describing the incident as unfortunate and unacceptable. “The Niger State Government condemns the attack on Lumma Ba’are community in Borgu Local Government Area, which claimed the lives of five persons, including the Village Head, Malam Bawa Muhammad. “The attack, according to reports received, occurred at about 5:00 a.m. on Saturday, November 21, 2026, when suspected armed men invaded the community amid lingering intercommunal tensions and launched an assault on residents. “Five other persons sustained injuries and were evacuated to the General Hospital, New-Bussa, where they are currently receiving medical attention. The Command also intercepted 828,920 tablets of different brands valued at ₦795.76 million and 627,320 capsules worth ₦376.39 million. nigeria.title: Rising profile of Tems, Asake and Nigerian artists’ Grammy journey
nigeria.description: By Ayo Onikoyi The voices are getting louder everyday that Asake and Tems are the new King and Queen of Afrobeats respectively. And the Recording Academy confirmed it on November 16, 2026 when it announced the nominees for 2027 Grammy awards. Asake appears just to be coming to his own with two nominations while Tems shatfers the roof with four Grammy nominations in one year. Tems has emerged as Nigeria’s most successful representative in the latest nomination cycle, earning four nominations and further establishing herself as one of the most versatile Nigerian musicians on the international stage. Her recognition in the R&B categories is particularly noteworthy. It demonstrates that her appeal extends beyond the African music market and that her songwriting and vocal abilities are attracting recognition in mainstream American music. The nominations also build on an impressive Grammy history. Tems won her first Grammy in 2023 for her contribution to Future’s “Wait For U”, featuring Drake, which won Best Melodic Rap Performance. She subsequently won Best African Music Performance in 2025 for her reimagining of “Love Me JeJe”. She has also received recognition for her contribution to Beyoncé’s Renaissance, Wizkid’s “Essence” and Rihanna’s “Lift Me Up”, from the Black Panther: Wakanda Forever soundtrack. With two Grammy victories already to her credit, Tems is approaching the 2027 ceremony with an opportunity to increase her collection and further strengthen Nigeria’s presence in international R&B. Asake on the other hand has not won any Grammy – yet. But he appears to be knocking on the door. The “Lonely at the Top” hitmaker has now received four Grammy Award nominations as of November 2026. His nominations are all in the Best African Music Performance category. His flirting with the Recording Academy started in 2024 with his hit “Amapiano” with Olamide, followed by “MMS” with Wizkid in 2025. nigeria.title: ‘I Struggled To Come Out, Lost My Sister, Other Relatives,’ Bayelsa Boat Accident Survivor
nigeria.description: A survivor of Friday’s boat accident in the Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State has recounted how she struggled to escape from the capsized vessel, saying she lost several members of her family and neighbours in the tragedy. The woman, whose identity was not immediately disclosed, said her elder sister, her sister’s daughter-in-law and two children belonging to her relatives and neighbours were among those who died in the accident. Recounting the incident, she said the boat suddenly capsized, trapping passengers beneath it. “The boat just fell and pressed all of us. My elder sister’s son’s wife was lost. My elder sister was lost. Her son was also lost. One of my neighbours who followed us also lost her son. My neighbour herself was lost,” she said. ﻿ The survivor said she was the only person among those close to her who made it out alive, adding that she struggled to escape after the boat overturned. “It’s only me that is safe. When I came out, somebody held me. I was drinking water. I was not able to come out. I struggled before I came out. Where we were standing, the boat broke from above and pressed us down,” she said. Asked by the Bayelsa governor, Douye Diri, whether the bodies of her missing relatives and neighbours had been recovered, she replied in the negative. Her account comes as the death toll from the accident has risen to 23, while 24 survivors are receiving treatment in hospitals. The accident occurred near Oweikorogha Community in the Ukubie area of Southern Ijaw when a boat conveying mourners from Ayama Community to Ukubie for a burial ceremony capsized at about 11 a.m. on Friday. ﻿ The Bayelsa State Police Command confirmed the incident, saying preliminary findings indicated that the boat developed a mechanical fault while navigating the waterways. However, a survivor had also alleged that the wooden passenger vessel, popularly known as a ‘love boat’, was overloaded with passengers and their belongings, raising concerns about possible breaches of waterway safety regulations. President Bola Tinubu has expressed condolences to the families of the victims and directed relevant federal disaster response agencies to support rescue and recovery operations. nigeria.description: Six league titles. Ten years. A stand at the Etihad with his name on it. Good luck following that. Enzo Maresca has to, after Manchester City unveiled him as manager back in June 2026. Maresca at least knows his way around the training ground. Back in 2020-2021, he ran the Elite Development Squad and won Premier League 2 with them. He returned in 2022 to work under Guardiola as an assistant, and that season ended with the treble. So this is spell number three, and he’s tied down until 2029. Expectations at City don’t reset just because the man in the dugout has changed. City’s title odds have become some of the most debated in premier league online betting markets because bookmakers must weigh a campaign shaped as much by events off the pitch as on it. A Flying Start, Then A Bump The opening weeks went better than almost anyone expected. Maresca became the first manager in Premier League history to win his first seven games in charge of a new club. The football looked familiar too. City kept the ball and wore teams down, which is no surprise from a coach who learned so much from Guardiola. His Leicester and Chelsea sides played the same way. City spent big to help him. Their summer outlay of around £460 million was a record for any club, and £125 million of it went on Enzo Fernández from Chelsea, a fee that matched the Premier League transfer record. Phil Foden signed a four-year extension. Rodri, one of the faces of the Guardiola years, left for Barcelona. Maresca has won quickly before. He lifted the Championship title with Leicester in 2023-24. A year later at Chelsea, he won the Conference League and the Club World Cup and still finished fourth in the league. Seven straight wins at the start of a season guarantee nothing, of course. Plenty of fast starters have slid down the Premier League table once the winter fixtures arrive. nigeria.title: Bayelsa tragedy boat had no manifest, passengers didn’t wear life jacket – Diri
nigeria.description: By Samuel Oyadongha, Yenagoa A visibly sad Governor of Bayelsa State, Senator Douye Diri, has revealed that the boat involved in the Friday fatal accident in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area had no manifest, and the passengers did wear life jackets. Consequently, Governor Diri vowed that all negligent persons involved will face trial. The governor gave the directive on Saturday after visiting the scene of the accident at the Oweikorogha axis of the river. Also, he visited survivors at the Government House Specialist Hospital in Yenagoa. He directed the Commissioner of Police, the State Director of the Department of State Services (DSS), and the Ministry of Marine and Blue Economy to commence investigation into the cause of the tragedy and submit a report in no distant time. Accompanied by Deputy Governor Dr. Peter Akpe, Deputy Speaker of the House of Assembly Michael Ogbere, and other top government officials, Diri in a statement by his Chief Press Secretary, Daniel Alabrah, condoled with bereaved families and affected communities. “On behalf of the state government, I extend our condolences to the families that have lost their loved ones and the communities that were affected. “I hear there were more victims from Ukubie community where the boat was headed, but several other communities were also affected. So our heartfelt and sincere condolences go to the communities, to the families, and the rest of the state,” he said. The governor described the incident as unfortunate and avoidable if every tier of government had done its job. “I believe that this should not have occurred if every department of government at the federal, state and local government diligently did their job. That is why I am going to institute a probe to ascertain what happened,” he said. Directing the Commissioner for Marine and Blue Economy, the Commissioner of Police and the DSS State Director to investigate, he said: “The Honourable Commissioner, within your ministry, there must be an investigation into this incident. “The Commissioner of Police and the State Director of DSS, I want a report; an investigative report on what happened. All those who have played one role or the other, the law must surely catch up with all of them.” Diri expressed shock that the boat had no manifest and did not board passengers from the designated point at the jetty in Ayama community. No safety measures He also lamented that none of the passengers wore safety vests, despite the availability of life jackets provided by the Federal Ministry of Marine and Blue Economy and the state government. “I cannot imagine a boat like that had no manifest and did not board passengers at the designated point. Today, we have this tragedy on our hands. “So, CP and DSS, you have work to do. I want that report in no distant date from now, so that people will know that there is a government in place here,” he said. nigeria.title: Pain of losing loved ones never goes away – RMD
nigeria.description: By Ayo Onikoyi Veteran actor Richard Mofe-Damijo, popularly known as RMD, has opened up about the emotional challenges of losing loved ones, describing grief as one of the hardest experiences he has had to deal with. The 65-year-old actor made this known during an appearance on At His Right Hand, a podcast hosted by Olive Emodi. Looking back at his personal experiences, RMD disclosed that losing his wife and mother remains a deeply painful part of his life. “Loss of dear people in my life is the hardest thing I have had to deal with. I have lost a wife, I have lost a mother. Loss is very difficult to deal with. The pain never goes away. “What happens is that the pain transitions, morphs into different things,” he said. Beyond grief, the actor also reflected on legacy and the responsibility of giving back, describing his current phase of life as one dedicated to pouring into others. “I am 65, and I am saying it’s your turn. One can always play an advisory role in nation building because you never stop building. I am in the legacy stage of my life. Just as people poured into my life, I think I need to pour into a lot of people’s lives,” he said. Speaking further about talent, the fashionable role interpreter maintained that natural abilities cannot remain suppressed indefinitely, insisting that talent will eventually find an outlet. “It’s a question of time. The stammerer will pronounce his or her father’s name. Same thing with talent. You can’t keep it down even if you try. Somehow, it will find its voice,” he said. nigeria.title: Death Toll In Bayelsa Boat Accident Rises To 23
nigeria.description: The death toll from Friday’s boat accident in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State has risen to 23, with 24 survivors receiving treatment in hospitals. The accident occurred when a boat conveying mourners to a burial ceremony capsized near Oweikorogha Community in the Ukubie area of Southern Ijaw. The Bayelsa State Police Command confirmed the incident in a statement, saying the boat was travelling from Ayama Community to Ukubie for a burial ceremony on Friday, when it capsized at about 11 a.m. A preliminary police report indicated that the boat developed a mechanical fault while navigating the waterways. Following the incident, rescue operations were launched, with several passengers rescued while others were initially reported missing. A survivor had also alleged that the wooden passenger boat, popularly known as a ‘love boat’, was overloaded with passengers and their belongings, suggesting that this might have contributed to the accident. President Bola Tinubu has expressed condolences to the families of the victims, describing the incident as tragic and directing relevant federal disaster response agencies to support rescue and recovery efforts. In a statement posted on his X account, Tinubu said, “Those who lost their lives in the tragedy did not deserve to die that way. I have directed all relevant Federal Disaster Response agencies to work together to ensure a successful recovery and rescue operation.” The President also directed that the presidential campaign rally in Ibadan, Oyo State, on Saturday, be held without much fanfare in honour of those who lost their lives. “On behalf of the entire nation, I mourn those who lost their lives in the incident and sympathise with their families, the government and the people of Bayelsa State. “I particularly mourn with Governor Douye Diri over this sad incident. I pray that God Almighty repose their souls and comfort their families,” he said. Meanwhile, Governor Douye Diri has visited the scene of the accident and is expected to initiate a probe into the circumstances surrounding the tragedy. nigeria.title: China Diaries: The Railway Connecting Continents
nigeria.description: Standing at the Xi’an International Port Station in northwest China, watching the movement of freight trains preparing to transport goods across borders and continents, I was reminded that economic development is not only about what a country produces. It is also about how efficiently it can move what it produces to the rest of the world. Xi’an occupies an interesting place in China’s history. It was once the starting point of the ancient Silk Road, which connected China to Central Asia, the Middle East and Europe through centuries of trade and cultural exchange. Today, the city is reclaiming that historic role through a modern railway network that connects Chinese manufacturing centres to markets across Europe and Asia. The China-Europe Railway Express is one of the most visible outcomes of China’s Belt and Road Initiative (BRI). Through this network, freight trains transport automobiles, electronics, machinery, textiles, agricultural products and other goods across the Eurasian continent. What makes the initiative particularly interesting is how it has transformed the economic possibilities of a city located thousands of kilometres from the sea. Xi’an has become an important international logistics hub, demonstrating that geographical distance from a coastline does not have to limit a city’s participation in global trade. The railway network has continued to expand. By November 2025, China-Europe freight trains had completed nearly 120,000 journeys, connecting 232 cities in 26 European countries and more than 100 cities in 11 Asian countries. The value of goods transported through the network had reached $426.4 billion by the end of 2024. These are not merely impressive transportation figures. They represent an evolving system of economic connectivity, linking manufacturers, suppliers, distributors and consumers across national borders. Beyond transportation: The economics of connectivity The significance of the railway goes beyond moving containers from one destination to another. It creates opportunities for businesses to reach markets faster, diversify their supply chains and reduce their dependence on a single transportation route. Rail freight offers an important middle ground between air and sea transportation. While it is generally more expensive than shipping by sea, it can be considerably faster. For certain categories of goods, particularly machinery, automobile components, electronics and other time-sensitive products, that difference can be commercially significant. It also provides an alternative when disruptions affect other transportation routes. Another important feature is the development of inland logistics infrastructure. Warehousing, customs processing, container handling, industrial parks and distribution services have grown around railway connections. entertainment.title: Asali Africa: Serves Up ‘There’s Rice at Home’ A New Cooking Series Hosted by Chef Soliat Bada
entertainment.description: Chef Soliat Bada Anyone who grew up in a Nigerian home knows the line. You suggest buying food outside, and before you finish the sentence, someone reminds you that there’s rice at home. It is usually the end of the conversation. In Asali Africa’s new series, it is where the conversation starts. There’s Rice at Home is a cooking and conversation show from Asali Africa, the Lagos-based creative development agency, hosted by Chef Soliat Bada . In each episode, Soliat cooks one rice dish with a guest, and while the pot does its work, the two get into the kind of talk that usually happens around food: family, money and what success really looks like. Rice is the most ordinary thing in a Nigerian kitchen, and the show makes a good case that it doesn’t have to taste ordinary. Over five episodes, released every two weeks, the menu travels from Jamaica to Saudi Arabia, back home to Nigeria and on to Louisiana. You don’t just watch the food get made, either. The recipes are written up in full on Asali Africa’s website, with the ingredients and method laid out step by step, so you can watch Soliat cook a dish and then make it in your own kitchen. The season opens with Rice and Peas with Oxtail, the Jamaican Sunday staple of rice cooked in coconut milk with red kidney beans (the “peas”), served beside rich, slow-cooked oxtail. Soliat’s guest is Michael Famoroti , co-founder of Stears, and their conversation turns to family and black tax: the expectation that once you start earning, you start supporting the people who raised you. Read the full recipe for Rice and Peas with Oxtail . Rice and peas with oxtail, from Episode 1 Soliat Bada and Michael Famoroti in Episode 1 Episode 2 moves to the Gulf for lamb kabsa, Saudi Arabia’s national dish, fragrant with dried lime and seven spice. Soliat is joined by Bella Adeleke , CEO of Asali Africa and founder of the fashion label Garbe, for a conversation about redefining success. Read the full recipe for Lamb Kabsa . entertainment.description: The presence of Mini LED tells a shopper something important about the light source behind an LCD panel. It does not, by itself, explain how that light is arranged, divided or controlled. Those implementation choices can have a major influence on contrast, black level performance, highlight control and the visibility of blooming in difficult scenes. From Presence To Performance That distinction matters because a category becomes more useful to consumers when it can be evaluated through clear performance principles rather than through a technology name alone. For Mini LED, three factors provide a practical starting point. The first is hardware local dimming. In a hardware based system, physical groups of LEDs can be brightened, dimmed or switched off independently across different areas of the screen. This gives the television more direct control over how light is distributed within a single image. The second is local dimming zone count and precision. A higher number of independently controlled zones can allow the backlight to respond in smaller areas, which can improve separation between bright highlights and surrounding dark regions when other major conditions are comparable. The number itself is not the whole story, but it is a useful indicator of how granular the backlight system can be. The third is backlight architecture. Full Array Local Dimming places controllable zones across the area behind the panel, providing the physical foundation for more localized light management than designs that illuminate the panel from the edges or operate the backlight more uniformly. Together, these three elements move the Mini LED conversation from a simple question of whether the technology is present to a more useful question: how effectively is the light being controlled? He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. Frequent questions men are asked: “How far? Work nko?” “When are you getting married?” “Have you bought land?” “How is the family?” And the famous Nigerian question that can make an unemployed graduate dread family gatherings: “So, what are you doing now?” We often inquire about their achievements, responsibilities, and plans. These aspects are important, but how often do we ask about their fears? A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. We admire their strength, we applaud their sacrifices, and we celebrate their accomplishments. But what about what they are going through? The person everyone leans on also needs somewhere to lean. Whenever I went to work, he would come to pick me up from the office, and we would go home together. In many ways, he looked out for me and made sure I got home safely. We started talking more. We would discuss life, share experiences and occasionally open up about things happening in our individual lives. There was also an emotional dimension to our friendship. He was interested in me romantically, I realised, but I didn’t feel the same way. I tried to understand my feelings, but the truth was that I simply wasn’t in love with him. I couldn’t manufacture feelings that weren’t there. Then I heard that he passed away. My first reaction, strangely, was guilt. I began asking myself: Was I a good friend to him? Was I kind enough? Was I considerate? Did I treat him well? Could I have done something differently? I caught myself wondering whether I should have given him a chance . Perhaps I should have allowed him to love me. But then would I have done that out of genuine affection or simply out of pity? And would that have been fair to either of us? My understanding is that not returning someone’s romantic feelings does not mean we cannot offer them genuine friendship, kindness and compassion. I didn’t owe him romantic love, but I could have been a good friend. That has stayed with me. Beyond the guilt, there was another question I couldn’t get out of my head: Why did God allow us to reconnect? Why, after such a long time, did our paths have to cross again? Why did we have to start talking, sharing experiences and becoming familiar with each other again, only for him to die shortly afterwards? Why him? Why at that particular time? He hadn’t been involved in an accident. He simply slipped and fell, sustained an injury, and bled out. His body was not discovered until three days later. Three days. entertainment.title: Visa Report Identifies Opportunity to Integrate Digital Payments with SMEs Business Operations in Nigeria
entertainment.description: Report identifies next SME digitization opportunity: connecting payments with day-to-day business management. 94% of SMEs surveyed find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, yet only 29% currently use one, pointing to untapped demand for tools that connect payments with business management. Integrated payment and business solutions can give financial institutions a more holistic view of SME cash flow and support more tailored financing solutions over time. Small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Nigeria have largely moved beyond the first stage of digital payment adoption, but a productivity gap remains. According to Visa’s new survey for its Pay and Get Paid 2026 report, most of the SMEs surveyed in Nigeria use digital payments, showing how firmly digital commerce has taken root in the country’s small business economy. However, many SMEs still manage the related financial and operational tasks separately, with only 29% currently using an integrated solution that connects payments with broader business management. The report shows that financial admin and disconnected tools create friction for SMEs, with surveyed businesses citing challenges in tracking outstanding invoices (14%), keeping payroll records organized (19%), and preparing financial reports (16%). These pain points reflect a disconnect between payments and the operational tasks that follow, with some businesses juggling multiple systems to keep their business running. The appetite for a more connected approach is clear. According to the report, 94% of SMEs find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, reflecting strong interest in tools that can bring payments and key business operations into one experience. However, adoption has yet to catch up: only 29% of SMEs currently use an integrated payment and business platform. The report points to several perception barriers that may be slowing adoption. Businesses cited that they already have manual processes that work (8%), that an integrated platform may disrupt their current way of working (8%), or that they do not trust relying on a single provider (7%). These findings suggest that broader adoption will depend on helping SMEs better understand how integrated tools can be relevant, accessible, and scalable for businesses at different stages of growth. At the same time, the experience of SMEs already using integrated solutions suggests a strong value case. The report found that Nigerian businesses using an integrated tool or platform report 93% satisfaction, with 88% reporting efficiency gains, including reductions in the time and effort required to manage their business. Beyond efficiency, integrated platforms may also create new opportunities for financial institutions to deepen SME relationships by using richer payments and business-management data to better understand cash flow patterns, support risk assessment, and potentially enable more relevant lending solutions over time. In June 2023, ahead of the 66th Grammy Awards, the Recording Academy announced the creation of the Best African Music Performance category. Its creation was a recognition of how far African music had travelled globally, and Nigerian artists were at the centre of that movement. From Burna Boy ‘s Ye , CKay ‘s Love Nwantiti , Wizkid ‘s explosive Essence , to Rema ‘s globally successful Calm Down and others, Nigerian artists became drivers of African music’s global expansion. Afrobeats – the umbrella term often used internationally to describe much of contemporary African popular music, although many Nigerian artists have rejected it for its tendency to limit the range of music coming out of the country – became an established genre globally. While Nigerian and African music have always travelled beyond their respective countries, the era of streaming and digital platforms has accelerated how quickly global audiences discover and engage with the music. African music became increasingly established in the West and other parts of the world, creating greater recognition for its artists and sounds. The Grammys’ decision to introduce a category specifically recognising African music performances was an important step in that direction, beyond the recognition African artists had previously received in categories such as Best Global Music Album. Although the creation of the Best African Music Performance category was celebrated throughout the continent, there seems to be a monopoly, or something close to it, of Nigerian music in the category. While South African artist Tyla has won the award twice, more than any individual Nigerian artist, Nigerian artists have consistently enjoyed greater representation in the nominations. Indeed, Nigerian artists are considerably more recognised globally, particularly in the West. However, I believe it is the responsibility of an award of this repute to look beyond the most visible names and recognise the best African music released within its eligibility period. The Maple Leafs take on the Columbus Blue Jackets on Saturday in what is a must-win game. If they are going to win, then they will need to do so without one of their veteran defenseman. Maple Leafs Scratch Oliver Ekman Larsson According to Maple Leafs head coach Jim Hiller, the team has decided to shake up its lineup by making veteran defenseman Oliver Ekman Larsson a healthy scratch. “Jim Hiller confirms Oliver Ekman-Larsson is a healthy scratch for Leafs tonight,” wrote TSN reporter Mark Masters on his X. Jim Hiller confirms Oliver Ekman-Larsson is a healthy scratch for Leafs tonight @TSN_Sports — Mark Masters (@markhmasters) November 21, 2026 We knew that the Maple Leafs were going to make some changes to their lineup after losing eight games in a row, but it’s still surprising to see the team give a healthy scratch designation to Ekman Larsson. Despite his struggles this season, Ekman Larsson has been a staple of the Maple Leafs’ defense since he joined the team two years ago, so this is a big surprise to see him as a healthy scratch. Maple Leafs Could Have Traded Oliver Ekman Larsson Last Year At last season’s trade deadline, former Toronto GM Brad Treliving was said to have multiple trade offers on the table for Ekman Larsson, who was having a great season for Toronto. But he decided to hold onto him instead of trading him. That looks like a big mistake in hindsight, as Ekman Larsson only has one assist in 24 games this season, compared to 8 goals and 39 points last year in 74 games. The Maple Leafs likely would have gotten a draft pick or two for him at last year’s trade deadline, but now, his trade value is gone, and the Maple Leafs may have to actually attach an asset to move his contract out following this healthy scratch. Ekman Larsson is owed $3.5 million this year, and next year, as part of his four-year, $14 million free-agent contract he signed after he left the Florida Panthers. The deal was looking good for the Maple Leafs at first, but not anymore. sports.title: Former Springboro HS standout gets 8-year, $95M extension with Mets
sports.description: New York Mets outfielder AJ Ewing, a former Springboro High School standout, reached an eight-year, $95 million extension with a club option for a ninth season. Ewing batted .252 with 11 home runs and 25 stolen bases in his first MLB season for the Mets. He was a fourth-round pick of the Mets out of Springboro in the 2023 MLB Draft. After SNY TV reporter Steve Gelbs visited Great American Ball Park in June for the Mets' series against the Cincinnati Reds and didn't have good things to say about the Skyline Chili cheese coney, Ewing came to Skyline's defense . Ewing had told Gelbs he needed to try a Skyline cheese coney while he was in Cincinnati. "You said you love them, and I found them appalling," Gelbs told Ewing. "Listen, Cincinnati isn't Cincinnati without the cheese coney," Ewing replied. "I understand that some people might not like it. I like it. But everyone that's from Cincinnati pretty much loves it. sports.title: 49ers veteran receiver’s recent departure hints at Mike Evans’ imminent return
sports.description: The San Francisco 49ers release Brandin Cooks to make room for a potential Mike Evans return. It’s unknown if Mike Evans will play in the 49ers’ highly anticipated matchup against the Vikings on Sunday, but the team’s latest move indicates a potential return. NFL insider Adam Schefter revealed on Saturday that the 49ers waived veteran wide receiver Brandin Cooks, which would create a spot for Evans. Mike Evans lining up at wide receiver in an NFL game. AP Photo/Jed Jacobsohn Cooks was signed to the 49ers’ practice squad as insurance to help what was an already injury-depleted wide receiver room as the team was without Evans at the time due to a hip injury. On Oct. 1, Cooks was promoted to the team’s active roster, a few weeks before Evans went down with an Achilles injury in Week 6 against the Commanders. This past week, the 49ers have been hinting that Evans could be active for Sunday’s game as he flew to Colorado Springs, Colo. , to practice with the team as it prepared to adjust to the altitude in Estadio Azteca — sitting 7,350 feet above sea level. 49ers wide receiver Deebo Samuel sprinting down the sideline. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Cooks, 33, primarily struggled with San Francisco this season, having only five receptions for 58 yards in five games. Before Evans was injured, he was the team’s leading receiver and was establishing a promising connection with quarterback Brock Purdy, having 27 receptions for 420 yards and three touchdowns through six games. Evans’ looming return to the 49ers’ roster this week comes a week after Deebo Samuel returned from a hamstring injury and had a two-touchdown performance in last week’s 46-40 win against the Cowboys. Deebo Samuel sprinting down the sideline. AP Photo/Tony Gutierrez It’s unknown what the future holds for Cooks. San Francisco might welcome him back to the practice squad after wide receiver Christian Kirk revealed on Wednesday that he had knee surgery on his meniscus. The team is also without De’Zhaun Stribling and third-year wide receiver Ricky Pearsall — who will be out for the rest of the season.

sports.title: In epic comeback, Monmouth beats Campbell 55-49 on last-second TD
sports.description: Destiny defied Monmouth. The fickle mistress of the football universe plagued the Hawks with officiating errors and self-inflicted mistakes in a crucial season finale on the road against Campbell . But with 39 seconds left and Monmouth trailing 49-47, she offered a glimmer of favor. Quarterback Frankie Weaver heaved a pass that could've been intercepted, and instead the ball bounced off a Camel defender and into the hands of receiver Christian Harrison at the 19-yard line for a 50-yard gain. That break of fate was all it took for the Hawks. Because they're not a product of destiny, they're a force of their own making. And individually, there was no more palpable force than wide receiver Tra Neal. On one final contested fade route, the star redshirt junior would not be denied as he caught the game-winning 17-yard touchdown, his fourth of the day, with 20 seconds remaining to complete Monmouth's incredible 55-49 comeback win over Campbell on Saturday. "This moment—it's as good as they come," Monmouth head coach Jeff Gallo said. "Our guys fought so hard. Resilient in how they finished the game. And they fought together in the fourth quarter specifically. We've had a lot of great wins in this program, and this is just another great one." It was one final instance in a long pattern of resilience and resolve from the FCS No. 20 Hawks. The two teams were tied 28-28 at halftime, but No. 21 Campbell (8-4) surged with 14 unanswered points to take a 42-28 lead into the fourth quarter. Monmouth (9-3) could have conceded after electing to go for a two-point conversion down 42-34 and not getting it, which beget another failed attempt later that left them down 49-40 with 8:03 remaining. "It all blew up in my face. I was aggressive the entire second half. We were gonna be aggressive though. I wasn't gonna sit there and let the clock bleed out," Gallo said. "We were gonna be active participants and win this game, all the way through. Sometimes it goes your way, it didn't. From the onside kick to the blocked punt to the two-point plays. But our guys kept fighting." It seemed as though another decisive blow had beset them when the Hawks cut the lead to 49-47 with less than two minutes left and then recovered a remarkable onside kick, only for the officials to call a non-existent offsides penalty that negated a play that would've turned the tide for Monmouth. But it didn't matter, the force of the Hawks superseded that ill-timed bit of erroneous intervention. Neal produced an exceptional effort in the receiving game with nine catches for 249 yards and four touchdowns. While Weaver was fortunate on that last heave, he was in complete control aside from that play with another spectacular gun-slinging performance that was somehow even better than what he showed the previous week when he was rated as the best passer in the FCS. sports.description: Credit: USA Today network via Reuters President Donald Trump has spent the last year championing Pete Rose and Roger Clemens for the Baseball Hall of Fame. But when he was asked about Barry Bonds on Saturday, his argument fell apart pretty quickly. Calling in to Fox News, Trump insisted that Bonds’ case is “different” from Clemens’, even though both players were accused of using performance-enhancing drugs. As he tried to explain the difference, Trump eventually landed on the claim that Bonds “just looked like he took drugs,” a comment which quickly sparked outrage. ‘It’s different’ Trump called in to Saturday in America , the Fox News show hosted by his former press secretary Kayleigh McEnany. McEnany, whose husband Sean Gilmartin is a former New York Mets pitcher, told Trump that her husband and her soon-to-be brother-in-law believe Bonds belongs in Cooperstown. Trump has long pushed for Rose, who was made eligible for the Hall after his death, and he issued Rose a full pardon for his 1990 tax conviction on Thursday. He has also called Clemens, a vocal supporter of his, one of the greatest pitchers ever. But Trump drew a line with Bonds, at least at first. “Well, it’s different. Pete didn’t take drugs. And Pete was Charlie Hustle,” Trump said . He then pointed out that Clemens has always denied using steroids, before seemingly realizing that Bonds has done the same. “And Roger Clemens said and stated strongly he never took drugs. Barry Bonds, I think, said that too. But a lot of— I mean, look, he was such a great player. You know, he was a great player before the so-called drug excursion, if that ever took place. But I think, and I’ll have to look at it, and I’ll consider what you’re saying too, by the way. He was— I watched him. The problem is he just looked like he took drugs. I mean, you know. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 21, 1676: Danish astronomer discovers speed of light — by accident — while observing Jupiter's moon Io
science.description: null On Nov. 21, 1676, the Danish astronomer Ole Rømer discovered the speed of light . Before Rømer figured it out, scientists thought that light travels instantaneously, or infinitely fast. Rømer disproved this almost by accident when he was studying Jupiter's moon Io . He was trying to figure out how long it takes Io to orbit Jupiter in hopes of using it as a cosmic clock. He watched Io disappear behind Jupiter and reappear on the other side. He did this over and over every 42 hours for years. To his surprise, the timing of the eclipses was not consistent. When Earth was closest to Jupiter, the eclipses happened 11 minutes early. Likewise, when the two planets were farthest away, the eclipses were 11 minutes behind schedule. Rømer figured out the pattern and made an accurate prediction for Io's eclipse on Nov. 9, 1676. Then on Nov. 21, he took his findings to the Royal Academy of Sciences and explained that a finite speed of light must be responsible. Danish astronomer Ole Rømer (Image credit: Wikimedia Commons) Why it mattered Understanding that the speed of light is a constant is the key that opened our ability to gauge the scale of the universe, as well as was central to developing modern physics. "The speed of light becomes a sort of ultimate speed limit," Live Science explained in an article about why the speed of light matters. "In fact, objects with mass, be they cars or neutrinos, can't reach the speed of light because they would need infinite energy to do so."

After studying physics at university, he became a journalist, swapped science fact for science fiction, and hit the jackpot when he joined the team at SFX, the UK's biggest sci-fi and fantasy magazine. He liked it so much he stayed there for 12 years, four of them as editor. 

He's since gone freelance and passes his time writing about "Star Wars", "Star Trek" and superheroes for the likes of SFX, Total Film, TechRadar and GamesRadar+. He has met five Doctors, two Starfleet captains and one Luke Skywalker, and once sat in the cockpit of "Red Dwarf"'s Starbug.  

Following the sad news of Sir Patrick Stewart's passing , there's been no shortage of discussion about his best moments as Captain Jean-Luc Picard . "The Inner Light"'s life in 25 minutes is a strong contender, as are the courtroom grandstanding in "The Measure of a Man" and his insistence (under extreme torture) that "there are four lights!" in "Chain of Command". But for this writer's money, it's hard to look past a nine-minute sequence in "Star Trek: First Contact", which turns 30 this weekend. With the Borg overrunning the newly launched USS Enterprise-E, Picard — who has long-standing beef with the Collective, following his assimilation in classic "The Next Generation" story " The Best of Both Worlds " — orders his crew to fight the cybernetic nasties hand-to-hand if required, defying their pleas to activate the ship's self-destruct system and retreat. He even calls Worf — not a man renowned for dodging a fight — a coward, prompting the Klingon to respond that, "If you were any other man, I would kill you where you stand." Ouch. But following some impassioned talk about making the Borg "pay for what they've done", he's finally talked down from his rage by 21st-century stowaway Lily Sloane (Alfre Woodard). She points out that his Moby-Dick-esque obsession is on the verge of going full Ahab, and he eventually sees sense, issuing the order to abandon the Enterprise and destroy the hive. It's a masterclass showcasing the ever-brilliant Stewart's impressive range, as the out-of-control captain's rarely seen temper reaches fever pitch, before normal service is resumed. His subsequent apology to Worf — "As a matter of fact, I think you're the bravest man I've ever known" — is simply perfect. And just as the franchise's zenith, "The Wrath of Khan", is built around Kirk and Khan's decades-old feud, "First Contact" is precision engineered to get the most out of Jean-Luc. This was the right "Star Trek" at the right time, a film that put "TNG"'s greatest villains on a collision course with the origins of Starfleet.
